title: Unbounded Resource Allocation in Collections
platform_conditions: Any Rust toolchain; Vec::with_capacity panics on allocation failure and the allocator behavior (overcommit vs guaranteed) is target-dependent
security_mechanism: Vec::with_capacity(n) reserves n * size_of::<T>() bytes up front, so a length field read from a peer header reserves gigabytes before any byte of payload arrives — one request exhausts memory for the whole process. read_to_end on a socket grows the buffer to whatever the peer sends, and unbounded mpsc channels or spawned task counts turn request floods into unbounded queues. Decompression repeats the pattern: decoding a small compressed stream into memory with no output cap amplifies a few kilobytes into gigabytes. Each is the same root mechanism: an attacker-chosen magnitude drives allocation or work before any bound is applied.

source_sink_clues.source: Declared sizes and counts from protocol headers, request body lengths, compressed stream content, and message rates from peers.
source_sink_clues.sink: Vec::with_capacity / String::with_capacity sized from input; read_to_end on untrusted streams; unbounded channel/task creation; decompression into memory without an output budget

tracking_guards: Check that any with_capacity argument is clamped to a fixed maximum (or sized from bytes already received) before the call, that body reads use take(Limit) or incremental reads with a cap, that queues are bounded (bounded channel, task semaphore), and that decompressors write through a limited writer with a byte budget.
not_candidate_when: The length field is validated against a protocol maximum below the memory budget before the allocation, capacity is sized from already-received data (chunked growth), or the stream is consumed incrementally with an enforced output cap.
synthetic_safe_example: if remote_size > MAX_ALLOWED { return Err(Error::TooLarge); }; let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(remote_size);
public_references: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html
CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html
